checkpoint_review: The Router correctly identified that the Head_and_Face and visible Body_and_Plumage checkpoints are present and testable. The classification of 'Body is compact...', 'Legs are straight...', 'Tail is docked...', and 'Gait is free...' as untestable is accurate due to the close-up framing, occlusion by the blanket, and the resting pose. I agree with all Router verdicts; no checkpoints were marked present when they should be missing, nor were any testable features incorrectly dismissed.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies (smudging) and minor structural collapse at the ear tip. However, the severity was underestimated. The expert animal_pose_auditor flagged a HIGH artifact risk (76% low-confidence keypoints), specifically affecting the limbs and shoulders. While the pose auditor warns against treating low confidence as definitive proof in AI images, visual inspection confirms that the front paws/chest area lacks distinct anatomical definition, appearing as a fused mass of white fur merging into the blanket. This validates the pose auditor's signal as a real structural defect (limb fusion/ambiguity) rather than just domain shift. Additionally, the eyes exhibit a slight 'glassy' or uniform specular highlight characteristic of AI generation, which the Router missed. The boundary between the dog and the blanket is consistently soft and ill-defined, exceeding normal depth-of-field blur.
alignment_reasoning: All testable checkpoints passed with high fidelity. The Blenheim spaniel features (domed head, stop, feathering, coat pattern) are rendered accurately. Four checkpoints were correctly deemed untestable due to framing/pose. Expert classifier confirmed the breed with high confidence.
